name: Cadmium
occurrence: Found as an impurity in zinc ores, recovered as a by-product of zinc refining.
majorUses: Rechargeable nickel-cadmium (NiCd) batteries (now largely phased out)
safetyNotes: Highly toxic and carcinogenic with cumulative effects on kidneys and bones — 'itai-itai disease' in Japan was a documented mass cadmium-poisoning event from contaminated irrigation water.
notableCharacteristics: Like zinc and mercury, its filled d-subshell makes its chemistry more main-group-like than a typical transition metal.
whyHere: With a completely filled 4d¹⁰ subshell in both metal and Cd²⁺ ion, cadmium shows little of the colour or variable oxidation chemistry typical of transition metals, placing it in the same 'borderline' group as zinc and mercury.
didYouKnow: Cadmium pigments once gave artists' paints their vivid, stable yellows and reds, but many countries have restricted their use due to the metal's severe toxicity and environmental persistence.
genZNote: Beautiful pigment, brutal toxicity. The periodic table's reminder that 'pretty' and 'safe' aren't the same thing.
